questions.q: What does cross filter direction control?
options: How far a filter is allowed to travel once two tables are related
Whether values can repeat on either side of a relationship
Whether a relationship is active or inactive
The order columns appear in a table
questions.explain: Cross filter direction is a separate setting from cardinality — it decides how far a filter choice propagates once a relationship connects two tables.

questions.q: With Single cross filter direction, what happens when you filter by a connected table?
options: The filter only affects the table doing the summarizing, not tables on the far side of it
The filter has no effect on any table
The filter always reaches every table in the model
Single direction disables the relationship entirely
questions.explain: Single is the common default — a filter choice reaches the table being summarized but doesn't continue past it to other connected tables.

questions.q: When does setting Both work well?
options: In a classic star schema — one central fact table with dimension tables around it that don't connect to each other except through the fact table
Only in models with exactly two tables
Only when every relationship is many-to-many
Both never causes any issues in any model shape
questions.explain: Both lets a filter continue past the fact table to a dimension table on the far side — ideal for a star schema, where there's only one path for it to travel.

questions.q: Why can setting Both cause a problem in a model with loops?
options: A filter could have more than one path to reach the same table, and Power BI can't determine which one you mean
Loops always disable filtering completely
Both direction is only valid for one-to-one relationships
Power BI automatically deletes one of the relationships in a loop
questions.explain: In a loop, two tables can be connected by more than one route. If every relationship allows filtering in both directions, that creates ambiguity Power BI won't allow.

questions.q: What's a common real-world example of a loop that causes this ambiguity?
options: A sales-actuals table and a budget table, both connected to the same department lookup table
A single fact table with one dimension table
Two completely unrelated tables in the same file
A table connected to itself through a hierarchy
questions.explain: When two fact-like tables share a common lookup table, that forms a loop — setting Both everywhere creates an ambiguous filter path that Power BI blocks.
